processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: 100 g alloy ingot (99.99% Fe, 99.9% Mn, 99.9% Al, 99.9% Cr, 99.8% graphite) prepared by cold-crucible levitation melting; remelted by induction melting and poured into a copper mold rotating at 600 rpm, giving as-cast strips of 80 mm × 60 mm × 2.5 mm. Near-rapid solidification cooling rate 1-1 × 10^4 K/s.
Stress relief annealing applied to as-cast strips before cold rolling ("cold rolled (CR) with 20% reduction after stress relief annealing at 400 °C for 1 h").
Cold rolling with 20% reduction (denoted "CR20%"), achieved by multipass rolling on a twin roll mill (Φ160); intended to eliminate solidification micropores and avoid great structural change.
Final step: the CR20% strips further annealed at 600 °C for 3 h in a tubular vacuum furnace; this condition is denoted "CR20% + annealed".

structures.overall_structure: Constituent phases are γ-austenite matrix plus irregularly shaped δ-ferrite containing an ordered DO3 phase (same assemblage as the as-cast strip); the cold-rolled (20%) strip retains this assemblage, and 600 °C/3 h annealing changes the 43.5°-45.0° double peak to a single peak, indicating almost all ferrite transforms to the ordered DO3 phase. High-density {111} planar slip bands introduced by cold rolling persist after annealing.

phases_present.morphology: matrix; smooth grey phase in SEM
irregularly shaped, blocky/vermicular, evenly distributed in the γ-austenite matrix

phases_present.crystal_structure: ordered BCC (space group Fm3m, lattice parameter a = 0.565 nm)
phases_present.morphology: ordered phase formed within the δ-ferrite; single XRD peak after annealing
nano-scale precipitates, mainly precipitated at dislocation entanglement in the CR20% + annealed 3Cr strip

defects.type: planar {111} slip bands (high density, retained from cold rolling)

precipitates.distribution: mainly precipitated at the dislocation entanglement (in the γ-austenite)

defect_interactions.interaction_type: dislocation entanglement at the ferrite/austenite phase boundary
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Dislocation entanglements occur at the phase boundary between ferrite and austenite, attributed to inconsistent deformation of ferrite and austenite during deformation.

interfaces.slip_behavior: High-density {111} planar slip bands introduced by 20% cold rolling persist after 600 °C/3 h annealing; slip bands are the main strengthening factor of the cold-rolled strips.
interfaces.phase_evolution: After cold rolling the constituent phases remain γ-austenite and δ-ferrite with ordered DO3 (consistent with as-cast); on subsequent 600 °C/3 h annealing the 43.5°-45.0° double peak becomes a single peak, indicating almost all ferrite transforms into the ordered DO3 phase, and κ-carbides precipitate in the austenite.
interfaces.interface_notes: No separate interface characterisation (coherency, misorientation) is reported specifically for the CR20% + annealed 3Cr strip.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: gage width 4 mm and gage length 12 mm, machined from the steel strips
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Tensile tests performed at least 3 times by a MTS Criterion 44 Mechanical Property Tester.

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress-strain curves of the CR20% + annealed steel strips are given in Fig. 9(b): 0Cr lowest, 3Cr slightly above, all curves terminate at lower strain (~19-20%) than the CR20% strips.

strain_hardening_rate.value: The strain hardening rate of the CR20% steel strips decreases gradually with increasing strain; annealing makes the strain hardening rates of the CR20% + annealed 0Cr and 3Cr steel strips clearly decrease at the early stage.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: After cold rolling with 20% reduction the strength of the Cr-containing strips exceeds that of the Cr-free strip (in contrast to the as-cast state): CR20% 3Cr UTS = 1270 MPa vs CR20% 0Cr UTS = 1154 MPa; the CR20% + annealed 3Cr YS and UTS do not change significantly from the CR20% strip.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Rigaku D/Max-2200, Cu target operated at 40 kV and 40 mA, graphite monochromator, λ = 0.154056 nm
characterization_methods.purpose: Phase identification of the as-cast, cold-rolled and CR20% + annealed strips
characterization_methods.key_findings: Constituent phases after cold rolling are still γ-austenite and δ-ferrite with ordered DO3 (consistent with as-cast); after further annealing the 43.5°-45.0° double peak becomes a single peak in the CR20% + annealed strips.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: After mechanical polishing and etching (3.3 vol% nitric acid, 3.3 vol% acetic acid, 0.1 vol% hydrofluoric acid, 3 s); photographs taken at 0.5 mm from the strip surface along thickness; phase fraction measured with Image-Pro Plus over ten different positions
characterization_methods.purpose: Characterize δ-ferrite morphology and volume fraction
characterization_methods.key_findings: δ-ferrite volume fraction in the cold-rolled 3Cr strips is 12%, unchanged by further annealing; Cr addition increases the δ-ferrite fraction.

characterization_methods.technique: Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM) with selected-area diffraction (SADP) and dark-field (DF) imaging
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: JEOL-2010F operated at 200 kV; specimens prepared by twin-jet electrolytic polishing at -30 °C and 30 V in 10% perchloric acid + 90% alcohol
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: BF/DF imaging and SADP along [110] zone axis; DF images formed from the (001) κ-carbide superlattice reflection
characterization_methods.purpose: Elucidate nano-scale precipitates and deformation substructure in the γ-austenite
characterization_methods.key_findings: In the CR20% + annealed 3Cr strip κ-carbides mainly precipitate at dislocation entanglement (Fig. 12 c,d); high-density slip bands persist.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Room temperature, constant strain rate 2.5 × 10^-4 s^-1, gage width 4 mm, gage length 12 mm, GB/T-228.1-2010, at least 3 tests
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure yield strength, ultimate tensile strength and total elongation
characterization_methods.key_findings: UTS of the CR20% + annealed 3Cr strip not significantly changed vs CR20% (1270 MPa).

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: AccuPyc II 1340 Gas Displacement Density Analyzer
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure average density of the steel strips
characterization_methods.key_findings: Measured average density of the 3Cr steel strip = 6.69 g/cm^3.

characterization_methods.technique: Inductively Coupled Plasma Mass Spectrometry (ICP) and carbon-sulfur analysis
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure chemical composition of the steel strips
characterization_methods.key_findings: 3Cr steel measured composition (wt.%): Mn 20.04, Al 9.09, C 1.23, Cr 3.09, S 0.0009, Fe Bal.

unmapped_findings: The paper states that the yield strength and ultimate tensile strength of the CR20% + annealed steel strips do not change significantly compared with the CR20% steel strips (b0064); no separate numerical YS/UTS/elongation table is given for the CR20% + annealed strips.

No κ-carbide volume fraction or average size is reported specifically for the CR20% + annealed 3Cr strip; the reported 4% / 4 nm values (b0071) belong to the as-cast+annealed 3Cr strip (a different sample), and the 7% / 8 nm values belong to the as-cast+annealed 0Cr strip.

The slip band spacing of 100 ± 15 nm (b0066) was measured on the CR20% (cold-rolled) 3Cr strip; annealing after cold rolling does not eliminate these slip bands (b0074, b0084), so the slip bands persist in the CR20% + annealed strip.

The abstract states the ultimate tensile strength and total elongation of the cold-rolled 3Cr steel strip were 1270 MPa and 21%, respectively (b0013); the highest UTS × TE product, 38.0 GPa %, was achieved in the as-cast 6Cr strip (b0040), not in this sample.

The X-ray diffraction figure for the CR20% and CR20% + annealed strips (Fig. 7) is captioned for those states but the curves are labelled 6Cr/3Cr/0Cr; this caption/label disagreement is noted in the figure description (figure_007).

A double (Slip-band and Microband) hardening mechanism is proposed for the strain hardening behavior of the low-density steel strips, with slip-band hardening active at the early strain stage and microband hardening at the final strain stage (b0091, b0099).

The decrease of κ-carbides caused by Cr addition promotes the formation of slip bands at the early strain stage, resulting in high-density slip bands during deformation and thereby a higher strain hardening rate of the Cr-containing steel strips (b0098).
